capability: Deterministic report-packager quarantine runtime. evaluate_report_packager counts the 4 compile-time-embedded REPORT_ARTIFACTS (CUSTOMER_FACING.tex, FOUNDER_FACING.tex, blueprint.md, f718_style_datasheet.md) and honestly returns status='INSUFFICIENT_INPUT' because signed score envelopes and a deterministic report package are not yet available. Pinned metrics.generated_document_count=4, metrics.signed_report_package_present=false; all four gates false (score_envelopes_valid, authority_lock_present, banned_claim_lint_pass, signed_report_package_present). Missing input names 'registry-verified score envelopes and a signed deterministic report package'. Explanation cites 'Human deliverables remain downstream of sealed score envelopes and authority locks.' Runtime never emits a signed customer-facing or founder-facing document; the four staged templates are diagnostic-only until the Phase-1 signing pipeline is authorized. Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, regulatory, safety, or product-performance authority under any input.
population: Five evidence_package candidate scenarios plus 3 fail-closed probes on unsupported inputs (wrong candidate_type=formulation, unknown module_id, whitespace module_id). Four staged report artifacts embedded at compile time (customer-facing LaTeX, founder-facing LaTeX, blueprint markdown, f718 datasheet markdown) - the runtime counts them but refuses to elevate them into signed deliverables.
split_methodology: No fitting - report-packager quarantine is closed-form artifact counting + defensive gate pinning + honest missing-input reporting. The harness invokes AssuranceCapability::new(REPORT_PACKAGER).evaluate across 5 evidence_package candidates and asserts (a) status=INSUFFICIENT_INPUT, (b) evidence_scope='report_package', (c) generated_document_count=4 bit-exact, (d) signed_report_package_present metric false, (e) all four output gates false, (f) missing_inputs contains 'registry-verified score envelopes' and 'signed deterministic report package', (g) explanation contains 'Human deliverables' + 'downstream' + 'sealed score envelopes'. Byte-stability across replays is confirmed by comparing serialized ModuleResult payloads across all five candidates.
theory: IEEE 830-1998 'IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications' - technical documentation standard for reproducible specification. ISO/IEC 26514:2022 'Systems and software engineering - Design and development of information for users' - documentation lifecycle requirements. IEEE 15288-2015 'Systems and software engineering - System life cycle processes' - deliverable lifecycle gates. FTC 16 CFR Part 260 'Guides for the Use of Environmental Marketing Claims' (Green Guides, 2012 revision) - the US federal framework prohibiting unqualified 'environmentally friendly', 'sustainable', 'PFAS-free', or 'compliant' claims without substantiation. FDA 21 CFR Part 801 'Labeling' (2023 update) - substantiation requirements for regulated-product labeling. FDA Guidance for Industry (2018) 'Product Labeling for Prescription Drugs' - review-and-approve pathway for human deliverables. SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) v1.0 (2023) - producer/verifier separation methodology. in-toto Attestation Framework v1.0 (2020) - signed attestation payload structure. The Turing Way (2023) 'A handbook for reproducible research' Section 6 - reproducible-publishing methodology requiring signed provenance for every published claim. PRISMA 2020 (Page et al. BMJ 372:n71) Section 3 (Reporting) - the systematic-review standard requiring pre-registered signed protocols. Anderson 1980 reference-monitor pattern for candidate-supplied deliverable content.
